definitions.explanation: The oldest son in a family. In traditional Japanese family systems, the eldest son had special responsibilities including inheriting the household.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{田中家|たなかけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{長男|ちょうなん}だ。
examples.english: He is the eldest son of the Tanaka family.
It was considered natural for the eldest son to inherit the household.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{長男|ちょうなん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{卒業|そつぎょう}→卒業：01643_sotsugyou⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{就職|しゅうしょく}→就職：03209_shuushoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧だ。
examples.english: Our eldest son is scheduled to graduate from university and start working next year.

notes:
Compound of {長|ちょう} (eldest/senior) + {男|なん} (son/male).

In traditional Japanese society, the {長男|ちょうなん} held a special position as the heir who would inherit the family name, property, and the responsibility of caring for aging parents. This expectation is less rigid today but still culturally significant.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長男|ちょうなん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧ (as the eldest son)
- {長男|ちょうなん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ (the eldest son inherits the household)
- {長男|ちょうなん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧ (the first son is born)

USAGE:
In casual speech, people often say ⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧ (older son) instead. {長男|ちょうなん} is more formal.
